item.title: Effects of environmental factors on the Mute Swan nesting density in marine habitats at the edge of range
item.description: Climate change has driven significant shifts in the abundance and distribution of numerous waterbird species. The Mute Swan (Cygnus olor) exemplifies these changes, exhibiting substantial population growth and range expansion northwards and northeastwards in Europe, with a tendency to form nesting colonies in Baltic Sea archipelagos. item.title: A new sub-horizon in the Albic Podzols of pine green moss forests: Quantity and quality of organic matter
item.description: After forest fires in pine-green-moss forests on the Albic Podzols, soot and charcoal transform the upper part of the whitish podzol horizon (E) into a grey pyrogenic podzol horizon (Epyr). In addition to pyrogenic materials, the Epyr surface layer contains detritus from forest floor and sand admixed from the soil mineral profile. item.title: Analysis of intraspecific variability in somatic embryogenesis capacity in <em>Pisum sativum</em>
item.description: Plant regeneration capacity in in vitro culture is of considerable importance for obtaining cultivars with required traits. Somatic embryogenesis represents a potential regeneration pathway widely used in biotechnology. In vitro induction of this process is challenging in many agronomically important crops, including pea (Pisum sativum). item.description: Endothelial dysfunction underlies the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis, in which there is massive infiltration of autoreactive immune cells through damaged cerebral endothelium into the central nervous system. item.description: The therapeutic potential of ribonucleolytic enzymes as antitumor and antiviral agents is well known. item.title: Nitric oxide and S-nitrosylation of proteins in cyanobacteria: The story is just beginning
item.description: Nitric oxide (NO) acts as an important signaling molecule in green algae and higher plants, regulating many physiological processes.
